verified_pass: Business-voice fix v2 — LIVE on fresh-p2wave-0903@aurem.dev. Sent 'what can you do with my GitHub repo?' as a NEW message. Real-model reply reads with clean grammar: 'I'm ORA, by Aurem. I read your actual site pages, find real problems, and publish fixes straight to your website's connection — you approve before anything goes live. Right now nothing's connected, so I can't inspect anything yet. Head to Settings → Website's connection or "Add website" in the sidebar to connect one, and I'll be ready to dig in. But I can update the text, images, or layout on your site instead — want me to do that?'. Checked against the previous-iteration failure signatures: NO 'website's pages is' (singular/plural mismatch — the reply uses singular 'nothing's connected' instead). NO doubled 'your your'. NO 'connection website's pages' run-on. The only stylistic sub is the acceptable navigation-label phrasing 'Settings → Website's connection', which the review explicitly permits. Screenshot: retest_reply1.png.

P2-F WELCOME greeting — LIVE on fresh-p2-empty-0903@aurem.dev (0 history, 0 installations). The empty-chat bubble renders the EXACT new plain-English string verbatim: "I'm ORA, by Aurem. I can scan your site for issues and fix them for you — just tell me what's wrong, or ask me to look for problems. What would you like me to check first?". No old jargon ('sovereign engineering co-pilot', 'what are we shipping today') anywhere on the page. Screenshot: retest_empty_dash.png.

P2-C softened NewUserWizard copy — LIVE on fresh-p2-empty-0903@aurem.dev, wizard opened via the /dashboard?action=connect-repo route + popstate. The account's ghStatus resolved to 'choosing' (not the pure 'disconnected' branch — same as previous iteration; presumably the useGitHubConnectStatus hook classifies a never-installed account as 'choosing' by default). The 'choosing' branch's copy is jargon-free: 'Install Aurem for your repos · One click — no token to manage. You pick which repos Aurem can see. Revoke any time from GitHub. · Continue with GitHub App · Opens in a popup. This wizard picks up automatically once you finish installing.' NO 'plaintext', NO 'plain text', NO ' PAT ', NO 'write commits', NO 'read your repos', NO 'password'. The wizard-repo-explainer one-liner 'A "repo" is just where your website's code lives on GitHub.' renders as expected. Source verified for the pure ghStatus === 'disconnected' branch (NewUserWizard.jsx lines 582-611): 'Connect GitHub once — this lets AUREM see your website's code (your "repo"), make changes, and open a request for you to approve before anything goes live. We never store your access key in plain text.' matches the softened-copy spec. Screenshot: retest_wizard_open.png.

critical_code_review_comments: business_voice_filter.py — the v2 rewrite (single-pass combined-alternation regex, longest-first) is a solid structural fix. Grammar was clean on the fresh live probe. Long-term nit still stands: word-level replacement is inherently fragile for tone-shifting; consider migrating some of the more grammar-sensitive terms (e.g. 'github' → "website's connection") to system-prompt guidance so the model generates coherent noun phrases natively. Not a blocker for this round.

rca of the issue: Previous iteration RCA (sequential per-entry .sub() calls letting one substitution's output collide with another map entry's pattern) was correctly diagnosed and fixed. The v2 rewrite in services/business_voice_filter.py builds a SINGLE combined-alternation regex (terms sorted longest-first) and does exactly one .sub() pass over the original text, plus config/business_voice_map.json now maps 'repo'/'repository'/'github repo'/'github repository' to the singular noun 'website' instead of the plural-sounding 'website's pages'. Both changes together eliminate (a) the cascading double-substitution AND (b) the subject-verb-agreement bug ('no website's pages is connected'). Live probe confirms both classes of failure are gone.
